To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TyrA is a family of dehydrogenases that catalyzes reactions in aromatic pathways, and its evolution is characterized by gene fusions, changes in substrate specificity, and co-evolution with other genes in aromatic-pathway regulon.

TyrA proteins are a family of aromatic-pathways dehydrogenases that have evolved in a complex fashion by gene fusion and by narrowing of substrate specificity, and that TyrA has been an integral part of a number of aromatic-pathways regulons that have co-evolved in a manner that is now tractable as a topic of research.

TyrA proteins of differing substrate specificities and with and without additional domains have arisen by gene duplication, gene fusion, gene loss and gene acquisition, with some of these evolutionary changes being associated with "jumps" in the vertical phylogenetic tree.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of the TyrA protein family in the context of the evolution of the pathways that lead to L-tyr.
the evolution of TyrA protein function, and we provide a framework for future studies.
how TyrA proteins have evolved in relationship to the evolution of the genes and pathways that they catalyze.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolution of TyrA has been complex and multifaceted.
TyrA is an evolutionary chameleon.
TyrA is an ancient enzyme with broad specificity that has evolved in a variety of ways in a variety of organisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TyrA protein family provides a model for how the evolution of gene fusions can be studied.
the TyrA family of dehydrogenases is a paradigm for the evolutionary dynamics of a gene family in the face of a variety of selection pressures.
TyrA proteins are a model of how the evolution of gene families can be analyzed by combining bioinformatics with experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the TyrA family is an exemplar of a protein family whose members have undergone a wide range of evolutionary changes, including gene fusions and gene losses, and whose phylogeny is therefore not straightforward to interpret.
TyrA proteins are not only interesting in their own right, but that they are also a window into the evolution of aromatic pathways.
TyrA is a family that is highly plastic in its evolution, and the phylogenetic relationships of its members can be understood only within this context.
